intended_object: The decomposition map attached to a subgroup tower J ≤ K ≤ G with right transversals U (of J in K) and T (of K in G). It is the bijection G ≅ J × U × T sending g to the unique triple (j, u, t) with g = j·u·t. Inferred from the docstring, the name and the module documentation, which is about towers of transversals.
explanation:
The body first applies `T.2.equiv`, Mathlib's `IsComplement.equiv`, which sends g to the unique pair (k, t) ∈ K × T with g = k·t. It then applies `U.2.equiv` to k, giving the unique pair (j, u) ∈ J × U with k = j·u. Finally it reassociates the product, so g maps to (j, (u, t)) with g = j·u·t.

The companion lemma `towerDecompositionEquiv_symm_apply` confirms this: the inverse sends (j, (u, t)) to j·u·t. So the definition is exactly the standard successive factorization along the tower.

The generality is right. It works for any group, any subgroup K and any subgroup J of K, with no finiteness or normality assumptions. This is the natural setting, and it is the same one Mathlib uses for `Subgroup.RightTransversal` and `IsComplement.equiv`.

Mathlib provides the one-step equivalence (`IsComplement.equiv`) but has no ready-made tower version, so this definition does not duplicate an existing one. It mainly serves as a tool for proving that products of representatives form a transversal. Still, it is a meaningful mathematical map (the unique factorization g = j·u·t), and it is defined correctly.
